svg.text: ☁ AWS Services — Interview Cheatsheet
COMPUTE
EC2 — Virtual servers, full OS control, many types
Lambda — Serverless functions, event-driven, no server mgmt
ECS Fargate — Serverless containers, no EC2 management
ECS EC2 — Containers on managed EC2 fleet
EKS — Managed Kubernetes cluster
Fargate → bursty/short-lived tasks · EC2 → steady/GPU workloads
Lambda limit: 15 min max, 10GB RAM, 512MB /tmp storage
Fargate Spot → 70% cheaper for fault-tolerant batch jobs
STORAGE
S3 — Object store: files, backups, static sites, exports
S3 IA — Infrequent access, cheaper, min 30-day charge
Glacier — Archival, minutes–hours retrieval, very cheap
EBS — Block storage attached to EC2 (like a hard drive)
EFS — Managed NFS, shared across multiple EC2 instances
S3 durability: 99.999999999% (11 nines)
Lifecycle policy: S3 → IA after 30d → Glacier after 90d
EBS only attached to one EC2; EFS shared across many
SECURITY
IAM — Users, roles, policies. Least privilege principle.
IAM Role — Attach to ECS task/Lambda to access other services
Secrets Manager — Store DB passwords, API keys (auto-rotate)
KMS — Encryption key management for S3, RDS, EBS
WAF — Web Application Firewall, blocks SQLi/XSS at edge
Shield — DDoS protection (Standard free, Advanced paid)
Never hardcode credentials — always use IAM Role or Secrets Mgr
Security Group = stateful firewall at instance level
NACL = stateless firewall at subnet level (both in/out rules)
DATABASE
RDS — Managed SQL (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, MSSQL)
Aurora — AWS-optimized SQL, 5× faster, Multi-AZ default
DynamoDB — Serverless NoSQL, key-value, single-digit ms
ElastiCache — In-memory cache: Redis (rich) or Memcached (simple)
DocumentDB — Managed MongoDB-compatible document store
Redshift — Columnar data warehouse for analytics/BI
RDS Multi-AZ → sync standby for HA failover (~1-2 min RTO)
Read Replica → async copy for read scaling (eventual consistency)
DynamoDB: design access patterns first, no ad-hoc queries
NETWORKING
VPC — Isolated virtual network. Subnets, route tables, IGW.
ALB — Layer 7 LB: path/host routing, TLS termination
NLB — Layer 4 LB: ultra-low latency, TCP/UDP, static IP
VPC Peering — Private IP routing between two VPCs
PrivateLink — Expose service to another VPC without peering
CloudFront — CDN with edge caching + WAF integration
Route 53 — DNS, health checks, failover routing policies
VPC Peering pitfall: route tables must be updated on BOTH sides
Public subnet: has route to IGW · Private: routes through NAT GW
MESSAGING & EVENTS
SQS Standard — At-least-once delivery, best-effort ordering
SQS FIFO — Exactly-once, strict order per MessageGroupId
SNS — Pub/Sub fan-out to SQS, Lambda, HTTP, email
EventBridge — Event bus, rule-based routing, SaaS integrations
Kinesis — Real-time streaming data (logs, clickstream)
FIFO: 300 msg/s (3000 with batching) · Standard: unlimited
DLQ → messages that fail N retries; never block the main queue
HIGH AVAILABILITY
Multi-AZ — Spread ECS tasks, RDS, ElastiCache across AZs
ALB health check — Remove unhealthy targets automatically
Auto Scaling — ECS service scale on CPU/memory/queue depth
RDS Multi-AZ — Sync standby, auto failover (1–2 min RTO)
S3 — 11 nines durability, cross-region replication
Circuit Breaker — Prevent cascading failures to downstream
RTO = how fast you recover · RPO = how much data you can lose
COST OPTIMIZATION
Fargate Spot — Up to 70% off for fault-tolerant batch
Reserved Instances — 1–3 yr commit → up to 72% saving
Savings Plans — Flexible RI alternative (compute/Lambda)
S3 Lifecycle — Auto-move to IA/Glacier by age
Right-sizing — Container Insights → tune CPU/memory
Redis caching — Reduce expensive downstream API calls
Cost Explorer + Budgets → alerts before overspend
OBSERVABILITY
CloudWatch Logs — Centralized log aggregation from all services
CloudWatch Metrics — CPU, memory, queue depth, custom metrics
CloudWatch Alarms — Trigger SNS / Auto Scaling on threshold
X-Ray — Distributed tracing across services
Container Insights — ECS/EKS metrics: task CPU, memory, network
CloudTrail — Audit log of all API calls (who did what)
Log → Metric filter → Alarm → SNS → PagerDuty
INTERVIEW QUICK REFERENCE
ECS Task Definition
Container image + CPU + memory + env vars + IAM role
Task = running instance · Service = desired count + LB
SQS FIFO Pattern
MessageGroupId = entity ID → ordered per entity
DeduplicationId → prevent duplicate processing
VisibilityTimeout → hide msg while processing (set > max job time)
My Approach
SQL (RDS) for transactional data · Redis for caching
DynamoDB only for high-scale, simple-access-pattern workloads
VPC Architecture
Public subnet → ALB, NAT Gateway, Bastion
Private subnet → ECS tasks, RDS, ElastiCache
Internet GW → public traffic · NAT GW → outbound-only from private
Common Design Decisions
Export pipeline: SQS FIFO → ECS Fargate → S3 upload → SNS notify
API throttle: ALB → Lambda → ElastiCache rate-limit check
Async job: API → SQS → Worker ECS task → DB update → S3
Scaling Strategy
Scale on queue depth (SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages)
Key Limits to Know
Lambda — 15 min timeout, 10 GB RAM, 512 MB /tmp
SQS msg size — 256 KB max (S3 pointer for larger payloads)
SQS FIFO — 300 TPS (3000 with batching)
S3 object — 5 TB max, multipart upload for >100 MB
ECS Fargate — 16 vCPU / 120 GB max per task
Common Interview Traps
S3 is not a file system — use EFS for shared file access
RDS Read Replica ≠ Multi-AZ failover (different purposes)
Security Group is stateful; NACL is stateless — know the diff
VPC Peering: NOT transitive — A↔B + B↔C ≠ A↔C
